A.name: Ali Amery
A.summary: Open with the greeting, read the opponent's source out loud, then react to it line by line with questions and repetition, and end flat on a fork. Keep reels to about two and a half minutes or less.

anatomy.label: Greeting + claim
anatomy.detail: السلام عليكم, then the claim in one sentence.

anatomy.label: Read the source
anatomy.detail: Their source on screen with the key line highlighted. Read it plainly.

anatomy.label: React
anatomy.detail: Rhetorical questions and repetition. Formal Arabic with some Iraqi flavour.

anatomy.label: Fork
anatomy.detail: You are free: if X, then Y. End flat. No call to action.

rules: Read the opponent's own source first, then react to it.
Use questions and repetition; stay formal with some Iraqi flavour.
End on a fork and stop. No call to action.
Never copy: insults, distorting the other side, filming real people to mock them.
evidence: 24 of Ali Amery's TikTok reels analysed on Meedro (October 2026).
Reels of 2.5 minutes or less: median 2.08x outlier score and about 53k views. Reels over 6 minutes: median 1.01x and about 26k views.
'Versus setup' hooks did best (median 2.08x). Plain 'bold claim' hooks, 13 of the 24 reels, median 0.96x.
Best reel: 3.4x at 125 seconds. Worst: 0.2x on a 5 minute feminism and hijab piece.

B.name: Challenge clip
B.summary: One pointed question in the first three seconds, the opponent's claim and their source on screen with the key line highlighted, one decisive answer, then the fork. No intro and no call to action.

anatomy.label: Challenge
anatomy.detail: One pointed question or challenge put to the opponent.

anatomy.label: Their claim
anatomy.detail: The claim on screen with the speaker named.

anatomy.label: Their source
anatomy.detail: The source on screen, key line highlighted.

anatomy.label: The answer
anatomy.detail: One decisive idea, two verified sources at most. Interpretations labeled.

anatomy.label: Fork
anatomy.detail: You are free: if X, then Y. Stop there.

rules: First 3 seconds: a question or challenge, never an introduction.
Name the attacker and show their words and their source.
One idea per reel. Only verified Quran and hadith texts with number and grading.
Voice labeled as AI. No call to action.
evidence: @orthodoxmuslim (Instagram): analysed reels of 36 to 118 seconds scored 11x to 16x outlier, 567k to 834k views, with question and challenge openings.
@korrathetaymi: median 66 seconds and about 71k views over the latest 20 reels, best 5.0x.
@bro_yusuf_11: best reel 6.0x at 54 seconds, a reaction to a named person's clip.
Hypothesis until your own 48-hour numbers confirm it.

C.name: Versus
C.summary: Open on a contrast: the opponent's claim next to the verified text, side by side. Resolve it in one beat, allow one light humor or meme beat, then the fork.

anatomy.label: Contrast
anatomy.detail: Their claim and the text, side by side on one frame.

anatomy.label: Their claim
anatomy.detail: What they said and who said it.

anatomy.label: The text
anatomy.detail: The verified source, number and grading on screen.

anatomy.label: One beat
anatomy.detail: Resolve it in one move. One humor or meme beat allowed.

anatomy.label: Fork
anatomy.detail: You are free: if X, then Y.

rules: The first frame shows the claim and the text together.
One resolution beat, one humor or meme beat at most.
Same sourcing rule as every style.
Fits reaction videos where the opponent's clip plays first.
evidence: Ali Amery's three 'versus setup' reels: median 2.08x, the strongest hook type in his 24-reel sample.
Lowest evidence of the three: small sample, one creator.
Hypothesis until your own 48-hour numbers confirm it.
